text:
Evan (AE): Quick heads-up — Acme Corp signed the POC MSA yesterday. They need: audit logs for all API calls during the POC, answers to section 4 of the security questionnaire (data retention + access controls), and guidance on whether to use Hosted API keys, a Dedicated pool, or a Private/VPC setup for their evaluation. 

Priya (SE): Congrats! For a fast start we usually give a scoped Hosted API key with token-level filters + 7d TTL. Works for latency/cost eval and no infra work. If they need network isolation or SSO, recommend Dedicated or Private. 

Evan (AE): They specifically asked for:
- full request/response audit logs (for compliance review)
- separation of logs per Acme environment
- proof of key rotation and ephemeral creds
- copy of our security questionnaire answers (signed)

Asha (Security): We can provide redacted request/response logs by default (headers, PII scrubbed). Full responses require a signed NDA addendum and approval from legal. For the questionnaire: I attached our completed answers and the control mappings. For audit logs we need to confirm retention window and where logs will be stored (customer S3 vs Redwood logs export).

Evan (AE): They want logs for 30 days and prefer us to export to their S3 for ingestion into their SIEM. Is that possible for a POC?

Luca (SRE): Yes — we support log export to customer S3 in Hosted POCs. Practical constraints:
- Export job creation requires an infra ticket and an access policy with the bucket ARN.
- For Dedicated/Private we can also write locally if they want no external transfers.
- By default we redact request bodies; if Acme signs addendum we can enable full-body logs for the POC window.

Morgan (Solutions): To scope the Dedicated pool: we need expected RPS, max sequence length, concurrency targets, and model selection. If they only want to validate quality+latency, Hosted scoped key is much faster. Dedicated incurs onboarding (~2–3 business days) and costs for reserved GPU hours.

Evan (AE): They're starting with a small eval: ~50 qps bursty, mostly short prompts. They also asked about audit trail showing which Acme user triggered each call (SAML/SSO mapping).

Priya (SE): We can include an ID in logs if they use our API with the X-Redwood-User header or if they route through their SSO-backed integration in Private/Dedicated. For Hosted POC I'll add guidance in the quickstart: set env REDWOOD_USER_ID per test harness. Example:
```
export REDWOOD_API_KEY="poc-*****-expires-7d"
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -H "X-Redwood-User: acme:user:alice" -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Note: never include real PII in X-Redwood-User in logs unless they sign the addendum.

Asha (Security): Action items from security:
1) Share signed questionnaire PDF (done — attached in the thread).
2) Confirm log retention policy: we can export 30d to customer S3 for the POC window only.
3) Provide proof of key rotation: we can issue ephemeral POC keys with TWL=7d and rotation logs showing issuance and revocation.
4) If they require full request/response storage inside Acme-only infrastructure, recommend Private (VPC) deployment.

Evan (AE): Great — can we get a checklist I can send to the Acme security team? Prefer a one-pager listing what they need to provide (S3 bucket ARN, service account, NDA addendum if full logs) and what Redwood will deliver.

Morgan (Solutions): I'll draft the checklist. It will include:
- Tenant info (org id)
- S3 bucket ARN + write policy + kms key id (if encrypted)
- POC duration and retention window (30d)
- Request for signed addendum for full-body logs
- Recommended integration mode (Hosted scoped key OR Dedicated if they want reserved perf + isolation)
- Dedicated onboarding steps and timeline
I'll post it in ~2 hours.

Luca (SRE): I'll open infra ticket to enable S3 export and link it here. Need: bucket ARN, IAM role ARN or temporary creds, and contact for verification. infra-bot will track.

infra-bot: Ticket RDW-1428 created: "Acme POC S3 audit export" — includes owner Luca. Please add bucket ARN and IAM role.

Evan (AE): Perfect. Also they asked about sample audit logs format — can someone paste an example snippet (redacted) so I can show the security team?

Priya (SE): Example (redacted):
```
{
  "timestamp": "2024-04-17T15:03:12Z",
  "request_id": "req_abc123",
  "org_id": "acme-corp",
  "user_id": "acme:user:alice",
  "endpoint": "/v1/generate",
  "model": "redwood-1-large",
  "input_tokens": 12,
  "output_tokens": 56,
  "response_hash": "sha256:xxx",
  "status": 200
}
```
Note request/response bodies are omitted unless addendum signed.

Asha (Security): I'll add a short paragraph on acceptable data types in logs and how we redact PII. Send me the Acme security contact and I'll coordinate the NDA addendum if they insist on full bodies.

Evan (AE): Contact is sec-contact@acme.com. I'll forward Morgan's checklist when available and ask for the S3 details.

Morgan (Solutions): Checklist draft uploaded: https://internal.redwood.company/docs/poc-checklist-acme (internal) — includes template policy for the bucket and sample IAM role.

Evan (AE): Thanks everyone. Last blocker from Acme was pricing for Dedicated during POC. Can we offer a reduced short-term rate for Dedicated evals?

Morgan (Solutions): We can offer a trial Dedicated credit for 2 weeks for qualifying deals — needs Sales Ops approval. Evan, file a discount request with expected spend estimate and I'll approve if it looks like a realistic pilot.

Evan (AE): Filing the discount request now.

Asha (Security): I'll wait for the signed addendum before we expose full request/response logs. If Acme signs, make sure they give us the S3 KMS key id so we can encrypt in transit+rest.

Luca (SRE): Adding one last note: for audit integrity we also provide an immutable event stream (write-once) with event hashes. If they want chain-of-custody for logs, we can enable that for the POC — it requires a config flag but we can turn it on.

Evan (AE): Fantastic — I will close loop with Acme and update here after they return the S3 details and the signed addendum. :thumbsup:
